 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Chicago Bears made a bold move by trading away two first-round picks to acquire defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons. This aggressive decision surprised many fans who expected the team to hold back. The front office chose to bet on a young core that can compete for years. General manager Ryan Poles sees a clear path to a long championship window. The team now has a defense built to support a Super Bowl run.
 This strategy relies on the fact that the roster is incredibly young. Quarterback Caleb Williams, receiver Rome Odunze, and other key players are all on rookie contracts, according to Yahoo Sports . This financial flexibility allows the team to spend big now without hurting the future.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Young Roster Creates Financial Flexibility
 The decision to trade future picks works because the team does not have many expensive veteran contracts. Most of the starters are still on their initial deals. This means the team has money to spend on free agents or trade targets without clearing massive salary cap space. The core group includes players like Caleb Williams, Rome Odunze, and Luther Burden. They all have years of team control left.
 General manager Ryan Poles understands that this window is wide open. He knows that by the time the team needs to restock its draft picks, the Simmons trade will be old news. Establishing a dominant defense now lets the Bears, a young team, maintain a high level of play for an extended period—a rare achievement.
 Other teams in the division have tried to win by signing aging stars. Green Bay paid top dollar for Micah Parsons last year, but their roster is older. The Bears have avoided this trap. They have built a team that can sustain success. This financial health gives them the power to make more moves if they see a chance to get better.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Defensive Line Upgrade With Simmons
 The blockbuster trade for Jeffrey Simmons changed the entire defense. Simmons is a proven star who can disrupt the opposing offense from the inside. The Bears gave up two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection to get him. This was a high price, but the front office felt it was necessary. The move signals that the team is done waiting for the future.
 Simmons joins a defense that already has a clear identity. Head coach Ben Johnson and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen have built a system that fits Simmons perfectly. The addition of a player of his caliber makes the defensive line one of the best in the league. It also helps the rest of the defense perform better by drawing double teams.
 This trade was the first step in a larger plan. The team is not stopping here. The front office has shown it is willing to spend draft capital to win now. The success of this deal will likely encourage more aggressive moves before the deadline. The Bears are proving they are serious about their Super Bowl goals.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Secondary Needs More Help
 Despite the big move on the defensive line, the secondary still has issues. The current starters have struggled with consistency this season. Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson have not played at the level the team needs.
 There is also a concern about depth. Rookie Malik Muhammad has played well, but he is now dealing with a toe injury. Relying on a fourth-round rookie to lead the secondary is risky for a playoff team. The Bears need an experienced veteran to step in and stabilize the unit. They have the flexibility to find this help without giving up too much.
 One option is Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen. ESPN's Matt Bowen proposed a trade for a fifth-round pick. Woolen has the size and speed to play man coverage. He fits the scheme used by coordinator Dennis Allen. This would be a low-risk move that adds immediate experience to the group.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Potential Reunion With Nahshon Wright
 The Bears are also interested in bringing back Nahshon Wright. He played for Chicago last season and made the Pro Bowl with five interceptions. He is now with the New York Jets, where he has no role. Wright told ESPN that he is "definitely frustrated" by his lack of playing time. He has expressed his feelings to the team but has not formally requested a trade.
 Wright knows the system and the players. A reunion would be smooth because he does not need to learn the playbook. He played all 17 games last year and forced two fumbles. The Jets are likely open to moving him since he is not contributing. This makes him a perfect target for a team that needs depth.
 General manager Ryan Poles has not been shy about looking for help. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, the Bears continue to investigate methods for enhancing their defense. Wright is a name that fits the profile of a player who can help immediately. The team could pair him with other targets to fill multiple holes.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Edge Rusher Options Available
 The defense also needs help at the edge. Rapoport observed that the squad has an obvious requirement for a pass rusher. There are two main options that fit the criteria. One is veteran Khalil Mack from the Los Angeles Chargers. The other is younger edge rusher Will McDonald IV from the Jets.
 Khalil Mack is a proven star, but he is 35 years old. The Chargers are not in playoff contention and might sell him for draft picks. A trade for Mack would cost a late-round pick. He would give the Bears an instant boost to the pass rush. However, his age is a factor for a team trying to build a long-term dynasty.
 Will McDonald IV offers a different path. He is 27 years old and was a first-round pick. He has 18.5 sacks over the last two seasons. This season he has three sacks in eight games. He has high upside and could be a long-term piece. Pairing him with Wright would address two needs in one deal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Tight End Situation After Kmet Injury
 The offense faces a new challenge after Cole Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury. Kmet was a key blocker and a reliable target for Caleb Williams. His loss limits the offense's ability to use two-tight end sets. The team now relies on Colston Loveland and rookie Sam Roush.
 Head coach Ben Johnson has praised the improvement of Sam Roush. Johnson said there is a "high likelihood" that Roush will see more reps. The rookie has only three receptions so far, but he was drafted for his blocking ability. The coaching staff wants to give him a chance to grow.
 Despite this, the Bears are linked to Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert. Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox called the Bears a "terrific landing spot" for Goedert. He is a Super Bowl champion on an expiring contract. A trade for him would cost a Day 3 pick. It would add experience but might limit Roush's development.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The trade deadline falls on Tuesday, November 10. The Bears have just a few days to finalize any deals. The front office is working quickly to address the needs on the roster. Coming off a 34-17 victory against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday, November 2, the team is moving forward.
 Now the team prepares to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. On Sunday, November 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET, Soldier Field will host the game. This matchup will test the defense with and without the potential new additions.
